card.name: Start of drug names in interaction sections
card.fires_on: The first or second piece of a drug brand or generic name that is split into parts, mostly in drug-interaction headings and sentences (section 7). Examples are the 'im' in Pimavanserin and the 'ab' in ustekinumab.

modes.label: Drug name in interaction heading
modes.description: Early piece of a split drug name at the end of a heading such as 'Drugs Having Clinically Important Interactions with'.
modes.example: 7.1 Drugs Having Clinically Important Interactions with P<<im>>avanserin Table 2 Clinically

modes.label: Drug name after 'with' or 'of'
modes.description: Piece of a split drug name in a sentence about co-administration or safety.
modes.example: Discontinue products containing disulfiram or metronidazole at least 14 days before starting treatment with<< dr>>onabinol oral solution and do not

modes.label: Numeric start of a reference
modes.description: The digit '1' at the start of a code in a list of agreements.
modes.example: 9/01/11 Consents of the European Parliament to the conclusion of the FLEGT agreements with Congo and with Cameroon - <<1>>2-14/01/

card.plain: It fires on the opening pieces of a drug name when the name is broken into parts, in the drug-interaction section of a label.
